newsitem.title: GERMANY: Frankfurt bourse ends at day's high, Bunds boost.
newsitem.headline: Frankfurt bourse ends at day's high, Bunds boost.

text.p: The Frankfurt bourse ended at the day's high on Tuesday, boosted by German government bonds which had risen on reports that Russian President Boris Yeltsin's heart operation had been successfully completed.
Apart from individual shares in the spotlight, trade was thin as the market held back ahead of the results of the U.S, election.
The DAX index of 30 leading shares closed floor trade up 19.43 points, or 0.73 percent, at 2,691.29.
After the floor close, the IBIS DAX, measuring all-day computer dealings in the DAX index, climbed above the crucial 2,700 point level, to trade up 22.40 points at 2,701.13.

Although Democrat U.S. President Bill Clinton is widely expected to win a second term, markets are watching to see whether the Republicans can hold onto their majority in the House of Representatives.
If the Democrats win a majority in the House, they are seen pursuing a less strict budget policy than the Republicans, which would worry markets.
The day's biggest loser amongst the DAX stocks was Germany's largest bank Deutsche Bank, which is due to hold an analysts' meeting on Wednesday.

Traders said there had probably been a large sell order from a foreign investor and the fact the stock had dropped below the technical and psychological level of 70 marks had also weighed on the stock.
Deutsche ended bourse dealings down 53 pfennigs at 69.77 marks.

Meanwhile, German chemicals and drugs group Bayer AG was up in line with the market, rising 38 pfennigs to 57.38 marks, after the firm published nine-month results within the range of analysts' expectations.
But chemical firm Hoechst, which reports nine month results on Wednesday, was preferred, rising 73 pfennigs to 57.83 marks.
Shares in German pharmaceutical group Gehe rose slightly after the company announced a renewed takeover bid for British firm Lloyds Chemists, offering 500 pence in cash per Lloyds share.
But the stock ended bourse dealings down 50 pfennigs at 101.50 marks, after competing bidder Britain's UniChem said Gehe could obtain less value from Lloyds Chemists than it could.
